reason: Re-read on 2026-11-16, after a second round of edits to this file; the digest is of the text after both rounds. This round changed: the front-matter dates and the Versioning sentence that says when a version counts as published; the printed set pinned to Unicode 15.1, with its seven named code points; the summary-line forms, which carry the exit code; the clause and the refusal for recording over a baseline, with --replace, two example lines taken from the vectors and a table of notes; the polarity rules for DeepEval and promptfoo metrics and the rows that feed them; --replace in the flag table; four exit codes and the sentence for a run that holds both kinds; the vector counts and the paragraph on the clauses that the vectors do not test. Each changed claim was checked against the tool source and the vectors by the tests in src/data/spec-*.site.test.mjs, which pass. Before this round the entry read: Re-read on 2026-11-16 after the edits below to the source and no other; the diff against commit f0f6819 is exactly these. How to read this specification: the sentence that made reproducing the vectors the test of conformance and the sentence that let a vector decide over the page are gone. In their place the clauses decide what is right and the vectors test them, a vector gives the words of a message only where the page gives only its form, and one paragraph says what a reader does when the page and a vector disagree: follow the page, say which vector is failed and why, and report it through the link to /contact, a route that exists. Values, sample counts and metric keys: the sample count of a promptfoo metric is the number of assertions that contributed a score, and the weight total never replaces it. The weighted mean is now stated in full, with a table of four cases whose values were computed from the rule and each confirmed by running the reference implementation: 0.666667 over 4 samples for a weight total of 6, 1 for a weight total of 3, 0.75 for a metric with no weight entry, and a refused metric for a weight total of 0. The new section The command line gives the verbs and their flags in a table, the default baseline path and, as Usage errors, seven numbered conditions; the row for exit code 2 of the exit table points to them. The seven conditions were written as code from the page alone and run against a copy of the reference implementation's source on 551,880 command lines of up to four arguments drawn from 27 tokens, with no disagreement, and each of two planted wrong readings made it disagree. Versioning lists vectors that are added or corrected to agree with a clause as an editorial correction, and the paragraph on vectors points to How to read this specification. The version is still unpublished, so these edits need no correction in the changelog and leave updatedDate as it was. Every other passage is byte-identical to the text read on 2026-11-15. The readings of those passages, and of the vectors against the implementation, are in the entry this one replaces: git show f0f6819:audits/phase-4.7/dispositions/spec.json. The built sidecar dist/spec/evals-baseline/1.0.md and page dist/spec/evals-baseline/1.0.html, from npm run build, were read for the new sections: How to read this specification, The command line and Usage errors each appear once.

The instruction to compare a copy with the digest is one the reader can follow with shasum -a 256. Re-read on 2026-11-15 after the move of the implementation checkout out of this repository. They are verified as operator text: each names the path it looked for and the declared value beside it, so a reader can tell an absent sibling checkout from a mistyped one without reading the source.
